text.content:
Anarch character creation follows the same five-step process as any other Kindred (see the core Character Creation and Traits rules), but the Anarch Movement's rootless, resource-poor existence shapes how each step is approached and what a Storyteller should expect or encourage.

Concept and Personality

Anarch concepts run from the politically engaged revolutionary to the simple street thug who never asked deep questions about why he joined a gang — there is no single "proper" anarch archetype. Natures and Demeanors with a special affinity for the Movement's causes include Architect, Autocrat, Competitor, Judge, Pedagogue, Idealist and Visionary; decades of chafing under Camarilla stasis or Sabbat dogma also draws Curmudgeons, Deviants, Rebels and Rogues, while Bravos, Connivers, Perfectionists, Soldiers and Tricksters make fine radicals for their dedication to acting on their beliefs. Even Conformists and Traditionalists can become surprisingly staunch anarchs if their conformity is to the Movement's own ideals instead.

Brujah, Malkavians, Nosferatu, Toreador and Ventrue make up the bulk of the Movement; Gangrel and Ravnos appear in smaller but notable numbers; Assamites, Lasombra and Tremere are rare (usually neonates fleeing their clan's power structure); and Followers of Set, Tzimisce and Giovanni are essentially unheard of, trusted by no one even when a stray individual claims sympathy for the Cause. Caitiff are extremely common, nearly rivaling the Brujah in numbers, and bring first-hand grievances against both sects' abuses.

Attributes and Abilities

Choose Attribute and Ability priorities as normal, letting concept and clan guide the split between Physical, Social and Mental Traits. Storytellers are encouraged to hold anarch characters to the letter of the rule that new Traits must be justified by in-game effort — anarchs have little free time or safe space to hone skills away from the watchful eyes of the sects, so a claimed improvement in Mental Traits might mean night classes, and a newly social Tremere might be learning to leverage words instead of rituals.

Disciplines

Anarch characters begin with three or four Basic Disciplines, as normal, and cannot exceed Basic level at character creation. Caitiff anarchs may choose Basic powers from any Discipline, though a Storyteller may restrict them to the eight most common (Animalism, Auspex, Celerity, Dominate, Fortitude, Obfuscate, Potence, Presence) absent a strong character history justifying something rarer. Storytellers are encouraged to be somewhat more lenient than usual about out-of-clan Disciplines for anarchs, reflecting the Movement's greater willingness to teach Disciplines across clan lines as an equalizer against the sects' resources and standing — though this isn't license for min-maxed "power combos," and an anarch's own parent clan may take a very dim view of secrets being shared outside it.

Backgrounds

Choose five Backgrounds as normal, but expect them to require more narrative justification and upkeep for an anarch than for a sect-aligned Kindred. Allies, Contacts and Retainers ("Common Ties") are the easiest for anarchs to acquire and hold, since they're generally earned through personal charisma, street savvy and hard work rather than vampiric lineage, and mortals who fill these roles usually aren't aware of vampiric politics or sect lines. Herd, Generation, Influence and Resources ("Uncommon Ties") are far harder: the sects guard Influence and Resources jealously and rarely tolerate anarch encroachment, few anarchs have the stability to maintain a large Herd, and even Generation can be a liability, since many rank-and-file anarchs instinctively distrust anyone showing an elder's power or a low-Generation pedigree. A player taking any Uncommon Tie Background should be ready to explain how the character acquired it and how she manages to hold onto it against sect interference.

Blood, Willpower, Morality and Virtues

Assign Blood and Willpower Traits per the Generation chart as normal. Many anarchs deliberately favor high Willpower, since the deep reserves of resolve it represents help a character keep fighting when the odds are against her; spending Free Traits on Willpower is a common and thematically appropriate choice. Anarchs are still nominally bound by the Convention of Thorns and the vast majority hold to Humanity; a character who instead follows a Path of Enlightenment should treat the transition as a personal subplot exploring the deliberate loss of their remaining human perspective, since few young anarchs are even aware of the Sabbat's Paths. When assigning Virtue Traits, tie each rating to a piece of the character's personal history rather than picking numbers purely for mechanical effect (immunity to fear, resistance to Morality loss, and so on) — the source material stresses that a Virtue score should say something about who the character is.

Negative Traits, Flaws and Derangements

Negative Traits and Flaws work exactly as in the core rules (up to five Negative Traits, no more than three in one Attribute category; up to seven Traits' worth of compensated Flaws). Storytellers running anarch-heavy games should apply extra scrutiny to a few specific Flaws: Infectious Bite is a serious liability for a group that depends on operating in the open without triggering a Masquerade crisis, and Territorial rarely fits the nomadic anarch unlife. Conversely, Enemy, Notoriety, Hunted and Sire's Resentment are common and reasonable choices, but a Storyteller should require that they reflect something more specific and dramatic than simply "being an anarch" — for instance, Notoriety should usually be tied to a genuine scandal or infamous incident, not just publicly known anarch sympathies. Derangements remain available for two Free Traits each exactly as per the core rules, with all Malkavians required to have one "active" Derangement for no Free Trait compensation.

Merits

Merits are chosen per the core rules. Enchanting Voice, Daredevil, Natural Leader and an occasional (quiet) Debt of Gratitude are all common, thematically fitting choices for anarchs. Storytellers should watch closely for players trying to justify powerful Merits like Iron Will or Unbondable purely on the grounds of "being a rebel" — much of the anarch struggle stems precisely from vulnerability to supernatural bondage and coercion, and removing that vulnerability without a strong in-story reason undercuts the point of playing an anarch in the first place.

Free Traits

Free Traits for anarch characters work exactly as per the core rules: five Free Traits are granted automatically at character creation, with additional Free Traits earned from Negative Traits, Flaws, low Morality/Path ratings and Derangements as normal, spent at the standard Free Trait costs. The only difference is thematic guidance: Storytellers should discourage players from using Free Traits to build an anarch who "has it all," since a character who is still hungry for more Abilities, Influence, Disciplines or other goals makes for a more dynamic, story-driving character than one who is only trying to protect what she already has.
